target_customer: Mechanical and hardware engineers using CAD software
problem: Engineers waste time on repetitive sketching, constraints and dimensioning in CAD.
business_model: Software plugin for CAD, free beta for Sketch Helper; later pricing not announced
product_category: AI autocomplete for CAD (Autodesk Fusion plugin)

founders.name: Sohrab Haghighat
prior_employers: Cruise (early employee, led Planning and Controls)
education: University of Toronto, PhD in Aerospace Engineering

founders.name: Kevin Chu
founders.background_notes: Also led engineering at SpaceRyde per R&D World.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs to understand sketch geometry and design intent inside a live CAD session with low latency, and integrate with CAD APIs.

defensibility.rationale: Deep CAD integration and usage data help; Autodesk can build similar features natively.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Autodesk was researching generative models; no copy of sketch autocomplete or acquisition found.

market_need_then: Engineers do repetitive sketch work; the company reports 1,000 engineers on its tool at launch and its site now claims 5,000.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain claims: 'You do the designing. Hestus does the clicking.'

branding.community_and_virality: Press in All3DP and Make: magazine on the free Fusion plugin.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear one line positioning ('autocomplete for CAD') and trade press coverage; the name itself carries no meaning.

outcome_analysis: Hestus is an active company founded by repeat founders from Cruise and SpaceRyde. It shipped a free Sketch Helper plugin for Fusion, reached about 1,000 and later 5,000 engineers, raised $1.5M in January 2025 and a $7.4M seed led by Insight Partners in October 2026. Founder market fit and a narrow wedge drove progress; Autodesk remains the main risk.
notes: Dealroom lists a $4.79M seed and some aggregators about $2M; conflicting, not recorded. The October 2026 round is called a seed by the sources. No competitor sources dated near the S24 batch were found, so the list is empty. Later entrants seen in Jan 2025 press: Autodesk Project Bernini (research model) and Bananaz ($5.3M seed). Backflip AI and Leo AI also appear in later search results. Name origin not found.
